text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When your code doesn’t work, the first step is to identify the bug. This means carefully reading error messages and checking which part of the program is failing. Instead of guessing, use a systematic approach: break the problem into smaller pieces and test each one. Helpful debugging tools include breakpoints, which pause the program at a specific line, and step-through features, which let you execute code line by line. Another simple but powerful technique is logging—adding print statements to see variable values at different stages. By staying methodical and patient, you can find and fix errors much faster.
